scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Kerala Natanam was developed by Guru Gopinath, a Kathakali-trained dancer, and his wife Thankamani Gopinath, the first student of Mohiniyattam at Kerala Kalamandalam.
They created a new teaching and performance structure drawing from Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, incorporating solo, duet, dance drama, and folk dances.
The style was named Kerala Natanam in 1993 at a global conference in Trivandrum, decades after its creation.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Kerala Natanam is performed in solo, duet, group, and dance drama formats, including Indian ballets lasting several hours.
It presents a wide range of themes from mythology to social issues, using expressive body and facial movements to convey stories and emotions.
Male-female pair dancing is a distinct style within Kerala Natanam.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costumes and facial makeup in Kerala Natanam are role-specific rather than fixed, differing from Kathakali's traditional attire.
For example, a dancer portraying Jesus Christ wears costume resembling Christ, while social dances use laborer or peasant attire.
Mythological and other characters have appropriate costumes to match their roles.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Guru Gopinath, the founder and developer of Kerala Natanam, and his wife Thankamani Gopinath, the first student of Mohiniyattam at Kerala Kalamandalam, are central figures.
Guru Chandrasekharan (1916–1998) was a classical dancer known for performing Kerala Natanam.
Kerala Natanam evolved from Kathakali and Mohiniyattam traditions, integrating elements from both and expanding them into a new classical dance style with broader thematic and musical scope.

images.description:
Kerala Natanam (literally Kerala Dance) is a new style of dance that is now recognised as a distinct art form evolved from Kathakali, a form of Indian dance-drama. In this photo dancer Theertha Prakash of Immanuval Higher Secondary School, Koothanellur, Kottayam performing Kerala Natanam at Kerala School Kalolsavam - 2024 held in kollam district.
